name: contract-model-identity
goal: Require the requested exact worker model to be reported; preserve usage and leave unidentified executions failed without fallback

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Codex task completions with no reported model are accepted by ModuleTaskRunnerAdapter.codex. Existing live Luna records therefore cannot prove execution identity. Preserve those original outcomes and close admission for future unidentified completions.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The existing model-mismatch case exercises only a different Claude model. Strengthen that unchanged case with absent and different Codex and Claude model reports, retaining original mismatch coverage and captured usage; add no test declarations.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Checkpoint dcf5302479: one existing case fails, eight pass. Missing Codex identity is accepted and mismatched actual identity is lost. Record a8c3a47b9654.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: The runner rejects a missing Codex model and retains the final provider identity on failure, alongside unchanged usage. Historical task outcomes are untouched.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Matched record a8c3a47b9654 fails one existing case; 2d8410341c19 passes all nine at 47e2bd5b1b. Same test bytes, command and reserved environment; no fallback or historical rewriting.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
